anthem-mdx-16.notes: Digital ins are PCM-only (bitstream mutes) — pair sources with a 2ch downmix. No HDMI/eARC.

anthem-mdx-8.notes: No coax, no line outs, no digital out.

anthem-mrx-540-8k.notes: Zone 2 line-level only. HDMI out 1 = eARC.

avpro-ac-avdm-v3.notes: Inline HDMI de-embedder; Atmos/DTS-HD → LPCM 2.0. The no-video-distribution bridge.

avpro-mxnet-1g-avdm-ev2.notes: MXNet encoder + balanced stereo de-embed in one box; no toslink/coax out.

avpro-acp-axis2.notes: eARC → Dante/AES67. Supersedes the discontinued ACP-DANTE-ETV (eARC + Toslink selectable → 2ch Dante, PoE or USB-C 5V, 1/2/5ms latency).

avpro-ac-mx-88.notes: Per-output analog de-embed is 2ch PCM only. PDF-pass 2026-09-20: 4x Toslink de-embed CONFIRMED (Markertek spec + AVPro cut sheet), 8x balanced analog 1:1 per output; extraction modes bind-to-input / bind-to-output / independent matrix.

avpro-mxnet-sw12.notes: 12 ports are NOT 12 endpoint ports: 8x GbE PoE+ endpoint + 4x 10G SFP+ uplink/aggregation. 370W PoE budget. SKU transitioning to AC-MXNET-SW8P — identical hardware, renamed to match the true 8-endpoint-port count.

avpro-mxnet-cbox-ha.notes: Official SKU AC-MXNET-CBOX-HA (TAA); CBOX-B = lower-cost variant; 10G-CBOX discontinued. 6 LAN mgmt ports, PoE-powered.

ubiquiti-usw-pro-max-24-poe.notes: MXNet on UniFi = viable, integrator-configured, not AVPro-qualified (~9W/endpoint PoE).

audiocontrol-m4800d.notes: No RS-232. 1 local analog per zone.

audiocontrol-m6800d.notes: Dante tx presumed 16 (flagged). MANUAL-CONFIRMED (M6400/M6800 user manual): analog inputs are per-zone stereo RCA (8 zones = 8 stereo ins) with hard-wired loop outs; the 2 bus inputs are DIGITAL (coax/Toslink selectable) — analog count corrected from 10 to 8.

audiocontrol-d2800.notes: LAN is control/DSP ONLY — never give it a Dante edge.

audiocontrol-cm2-750d.notes: Per-ch 70V/100V or 8/4Ω, 750W/ch @70V — the landscape workhorse. Analog counts flagged on CM2/3.

audiocontrol-bijou-3100.notes: Compact zone amp with eARC in — a TV-return path. Outputs: 1 sub + 2 assignable line/preamp outs (headphone/BT-adapter downmix tap).

savant-avb-output-module.notes: CORRECTED verified flag only (port count was already right). Legacy AVB backplane output card — 8 stereo pairs / 16 RCA jacks unbalanced (AOM-D16U-00, also branded AOM-016U) or 8 balanced stereo pairs on screw-down connectors (AOM-BAL16-00). Pre-amp/line level only, no on-board amplification. Lives in a Savant SVS rack chassis. Still fielded; NOT the current spec path — see savant-pav-aom8c.

savant-avb-input-module.notes: CORRECTED (was inputs: {analog:8, optical:2}, verified:false). This is the legacy AVB backplane input card — 8 unbalanced stereo RCA inputs (AIM-0A16-05, 16 RCA jacks) or 8 balanced stereo inputs (AIM-BAL16-01). PURE ANALOG — no coax, no optical, no digital of any kind; the optical:2 in the old placeholder was never real on this SKU. Lives in a Savant SVS rack chassis, no PoE, no standalone control ports. Still fielded in older installs; NOT what Savant sells for new AVB audio designs — see savant-pav-aim7c for the current spec path.

sonance-blaze-pzc-508.notes: 1U, 60W/ch @4/8Ω Lo-Z (500W total) or 125W/ch Hi-Z (70V/100V). 8 balanced Euroblock + 8 unbalanced RCA analog inputs (paired 1:1 with channels), full-matrix DSP via PowerZone Control web app. No Dante — use 1008D for that. Non-bridging model (see 1008 for BTL power).

sonance-blaze-pzc-1008d.notes: 1U, 125W/ch Lo-Z (1000W total) or 250W/ch Hi-Z 70V/100V. 8 balanced Euroblock + 8 unbalanced RCA analog inputs. GOTCHA: Dante is a fixed Ultimo 4x4 chip regardless of amp channel count — an 8-channel amp only gets 4 Dante channels in/out, not 8. Full-matrix DSP via PowerZone Control web app.

sonance-blaze-pzc-2004d.notes: 2U full-rack, 500W/ch SE or 1000W/ch bridged (BTL), 1000W @70V/100V. Dante Ultimo 4x4 chip — matches the 4 amp channels exactly here (unlike the 1008D).

sonance-blaze-pzc-6008d.notes: 2U full-rack flagship, 750W/ch SE or 1500W/ch bridged (BTL), 1200W @70V/100V. Same Dante-4x4-on-8-channel gotcha as the 1008D. 6000W total system power — verify house electrical service before spec'ing multiples.

sonance-dsp-2-150-mkiii.notes: MANUAL-CONFIRMED (2023 DSP 2-150 MKIII manual + datasheet): factory Hybrid Input/Output Module = 1 stereo RCA analog in + loop out + 1 coax + 1 Toslink — USE ONLY ONE INPUT TYPE at a time (selectable, not simultaneous sources). 150W/ch @8Ω, 224W @4Ω, bridged 473W. SonARC v2 DSP. Half-width 1U.

sonance-dsp-8-130-mkiii.notes: MANUAL-CONFIRMED (2023 DSP 8-130 MKIII manual): rear panel carries 4 stereo RCA analog input pairs STANDARD (1L-4L/1R-4R — all 8 channels fed as 4 stereo sources) + non-buffered loop outs. CORRECTS the distributor claim of shipping half-populated. Manual prose references coax/optical digital inputs but the rear-panel figure shows analog only — digital arrives via optional DIM/HIM modules, count unpublished. 130W/ch Class-D, stable to 2Ω, bridgeable. 1RU.

sonance-dsp-2-750-mkiii.notes: MANUAL-CONFIRMED (2023 DSP 2-750 MKIII manual, rear-panel diagram): analog stereo in + loop out + 1 coax + 1 Toslink — 'Use Only One Type Of Input Connection'. 750W/ch @4Ω or 70V (70V is default mode), bridgeable. The landscape/garden workhorse — pairs with Sonance Garden Series (8 sats + 1 sub per amp, expandable 16+2).

audiocontrol-acp-dante-d-poe.notes: Dante → legacy analog endpoint (the decoder counterpart to the ACP-DANTE-E-POE already in the catalog). 1x stereo RCA analog out. PoE or USB-C 5V. Configurable 1/2/5ms latency.

avpro-mxnet-1g-ev2.notes: Standard (non-downmixing) MXNet 1G Evolution II encoder. HDMI loop-out + balanced stereo analog de-embed (5-pin Phoenix) + Toslink. GOTCHA: Toslink is currently 'Future Audio Return Support Only' — eARC/ARC not active yet. This is a straight PCM de-embed, not a Dolby/DTS downmixer — use the AC-MXNET-1G-AVDM-EV2 (already in catalog) for Atmos/DTS-HD → 2ch. PoE 802.3af (15.4W).

avpro-mxnet-1g-dv2.notes: Standard MXNet 1G Evolution II decoder. 1x HDMI out, balanced stereo analog de-embed, Toslink (same 'future ARC support only' caveat as the EV2 encoder — no active downmix/eARC today). PoE 802.3af (15.4W).

avpro-mxnet-sw24.notes: DISCONTINUED (AVPro Global) — replaced by AC-MXNET-SW24P (same 24x GbE PoE+ + 4x 10G SFP+). 370W PoE budget confirmed. Still fielded; for new designs spec the SW24P, or the SW24E economy variant (Layer 2.5, 4x 1G SFP stacking, also 370W).

avpro-ac-mx-44.notes: 4x4, 18Gbps, dual audio de-embed (Toslink 7CH + balanced analog 2CH, same family architecture as AC-MX-88) — PDF pass 2026-09-20 confirmed the port TYPES but no text source publishes the per-output COUNTS for this SKU; the last remaining unverified AVPro spec. Check the rear panel before relying on de-embed counts.

avpro-ac-mx-1616.notes: CONFIRMED (Markertek AC-MX-1616 Gen 2 spec): 16x16 HDMI 18Gbps, 16x balanced analog de-embed (5-pin terminal, ships with 16 extraction cables), 3 extraction modes (bind input / bind output / independent matrix). NO Toslink/coax digital de-embed — the distributor 'digital coax outputs' blurb was wrong.

savant-pav-aim7c.notes: CURRENT Savant spec path for local-source-to-AVB-network audio input, replacing the legacy AIM-0A16 backplane card. "7 Source Audio Input IP Transmitter": 3x analog stereo RCA + 2x coax S/PDIF + 2x optical Toslink = 7 total sources, encoded and sent over a standard AVB-capable IP network (no proprietary backplane). Standalone PoE-powered box, not a rack card. Also has 2x RS-232 + 6x IR control ports for source control. GOTCHA: nearly 3x fewer analog inputs than the legacy card it replaces — a straight 1:1 module swap on an existing job will likely come up short on analog sources.

savant-pav-aom8c.notes: CURRENT Savant spec path for AVB-network-to-zone audio output, replacing the legacy AOM-D16U backplane card. Marketed as "16-Channel Audio Output IP Receiver" = 8 stereo pairs, unbalanced RCA/screw-terminal, any-stream-to-any-output routing. Receives up to 8 AVB streams from the network and can route any stream to any of the 8 stereo outputs (matrix-style, not fixed-assignment). PoE, max 15W draw (fits 802.3af). Supports mute/volume/PEQ/mono-sum/up to 160ms delay per output, plus GPIO to trigger an external amp. Balanced version: see savant-pav-aombal8c.

savant-pav-aombal8c.notes: Balanced-output sibling of the PAV-AOM8C-00 — same 8-stereo-pair count and up-to-8-stream AVB routing, but 8 stereo pairs of balanced (Euroblock/screw-down) output instead of unbalanced RCA. Use for long commercial runs or noisy electrical environments.

savant-ip-audio-125.notes: All-in-one amplified host: 4 amplified zones @125W/ch + 2 pre-amp (line-level) zones, built-in Savant Music 2.0 server (1 stream), functions as an Ecosystem/IP-Audio-Host-tier host for licensing purposes. 2U rack-mountable. Scales with additional units behind a Smart/Pro Host and a supported AVB switch. verified:false because the exact pre-amp zone output connector split (1 RCA + 1 Toslink, by analogy with the confirmed IP Audio 50 V2 spec below) was not independently confirmed for the 125 specifically — confirm from the official QRG (009-1584-01) before relying on the outputs field.

savant-ip-audio-50v2.notes: All-in-one amplified host, smaller sibling of the IP Audio 125: 4 amplified zones @50W/ch (rated, 8Ω) + 2 pre-amp zones (one RCA, one Toslink out — explicitly confirmed, not the same zone). 4 local audio inputs (2 analog + 2 digital) feeding the amp/AVB network in addition to whatever arrives over AVB. Built-in Savant Music 2.0 server. Max power draw 225W.

savant-pav-sms2001.notes: All-native AVB music streamer/source — 1x Ethernet port carries AVB to feed amps/AOMs directly over the network, plus 1x physical coax and 1x physical optical output for feeding a legacy (non-AVB) zone amp or AVR directly. PoE, max 15W. Supersedes the legacy SMS-1001/SMS-100AM single-stream servers and the older SMS-002A SmartMedia Server (500GB local storage, 2 simultaneous streams — EOL, see Unresolved).

sonos-amp.notes: One stereo zone, 2 amplified channels. 125W/ch RMS @8Ω (0.1% THD), roughly doubles into 4Ω (4Ω minimum load) — GOTCHA: several retailers title the SKU '250W' (125x2 summed, not per-channel); don't let that inflate a per-channel power figure in capacity math. 1x HDMI **ARC** input (not eARC) for TV sound — note the Amp is 2-channel only, so even over ARC it plays TV audio as a stereo downmix, no Atmos object/height decoding (contrast with the Arc Ultra/Beam Gen 2 soundbars below, which DO decode Atmos because they have the driver array for it). 1x stereo RCA line-in (turntable/CD), shareable/groupable to play on other Sonos rooms subject to the same 75ms line-in buffering as the Port (see headline note above). Auto-detecting sub output, adjustable 50–110Hz crossover. Dual 10/100 Ethernet (NOT gigabit — irrelevant for the Amp's own low-bitrate audio stream, but a hard ceiling if daisy-chaining other gear off it) or WiFi. Each of the 2 channels can drive 2 pairs of 8Ω speakers wired in parallel (4Ω net) — i.e. up to 4 speakers total (2 pairs) off one Amp, but they're all ONE volume zone; a second physical area needing independent volume needs its own Amp or a volume-control speaker selector downstream. NO 70V/100V capability — confirmed absent from every spec source found; Sonos amps are low-Z consumer-grade only, never spec this for a 70V distributed run.

sonos-port.notes: Bidirectional bridge box, not just a one-way source: the SAME unit simultaneously (a) ingests a legacy analog source (turntable, CD player, an AVR's 2ch preout) via its 1x stereo RCA line-in and makes it available/groupable across the Sonos system, AND (b) decodes whatever the Sonos system is playing back out to a legacy zone amp/receiver via 1x stereo RCA line-out + 1x digital coax out (NO optical out — coax only). Also has a 12V trigger output (200mA) to power on a downstream amp, not counted in the port totals above. Dual 10/100 Ethernet, no PoE. LIP-SYNC GOTCHA (see headline note): minimum 75ms buffered latency on the line-in path the moment it's grouped with other rooms, by design, for multiroom sync — stacks with the TV's own ~100–150ms video-processing delay if used to encode TV audio. Sonos added Group Audio Delay + Audio Delay compensation settings in app/firmware 10.6.2 specifically for this; treat as 'viable with per-room tuning,' not 'automatically lip-synced out of the box.' No successor SKU found as of this research date — 'Port 2' appears to be unfounded/no active rumor (see Unresolved).

sonos-arc-ultra.notes: Current flagship soundbar. Single HDMI eARC port ONLY — no HDMI inputs of any kind, no optical, no analog. Every external source must be routed through the TV and back down the single eARC connection; you cannot patch a second source directly into the bar. 9.1.4-channel driver array (up to that config with 2x Era 300 surrounds + Sub 4). Bluetooth streaming supported as a secondary input path. Pairs with Sub 4 and Era 100/300 as surrounds (see those entries) — when an Era is bonded as a surround, its own line-in is disabled (see sonos-era-300 notes).

sonos-beam-gen2.notes: Mid-tier soundbar. Single HDMI eARC input (backward compatible with ARC-only TVs). Ships with an optical adapter in the box for TVs with no ARC/eARC — GOTCHA: using the optical adapter drops Dolby Atmos entirely (optical can't carry the Dolby Digital Plus/TrueHD bitstream Atmos needs), falls back to 5.1/stereo. Has its own Ethernet port for wired network. 5.0.2-channel driver array; supports Atmos via HDMI eARC/ARC using Dolby Digital Plus (lossy) or, over eARC only, Dolby TrueHD (lossless). NOTE 2026-09: Beam Ultra ($699, ships 9/29) supersedes at the mid-tier — check whether Gen 2 continues at a lower price before quoting.

sonos-ray.notes: Budget/entry soundbar. NO HDMI at all — optical (Toslink) digital input only, ships with the optical cable in box. No eARC/ARC means no Dolby Atmos support — format ceiling is Stereo PCM, Dolby Digital 5.1, DTS Digital Surround. Has a built-in IR receiver so the TV's own remote still controls volume/power despite no HDMI-CEC link. Has its own Ethernet port. Good fit for a secondary/bedroom TV zone where the budget doesn't support eARC gear; wrong choice anywhere Atmos or multi-source HDMI switching matters.

sonos-sub4.notes: Wireless subwoofer, no line-level or HDMI ports at all — pairs over WiFi (802.11a/b/g/n/ac/ax) to an Arc Ultra/Arc/Beam or a stereo pair; has an optional 10/100 Ethernet port for a wired network connection but nothing an integrator patches into. Dual force-cancelling 5x8" woofers, ~25Hz extension, dual Class-D amps on board. Zero port-capacity relevance for the trunk checker — included here purely so the BOM/notes list doesn't have to invent a device for it.

sonos-era-300-surround.notes: Line-in requires a separately-sold USB-C adapter (Sonos Line-In Adapter: 3.5mm-to-USB-C, or the Combo Adapter which adds an Ethernet port) — there is no line-in jack on the speaker itself. GOTCHA: line-in is automatically DISABLED whenever the Era 300 is bonded as a home-theater surround speaker (paired behind an Arc/Arc Ultra/Beam) — you cannot use a surround-paired Era 300 as a line-in zone at the same time; it's one role or the other. Two Era 300s pair as rear surrounds for Atmos height content.

sonos-era-100-surround.notes: Same line-in-via-separately-sold-USB-C-adapter and same surround-disables-line-in gotcha as the Era 300 (see that entry). Smaller/cheaper stereo bookshelf speaker, used as budget surrounds behind a Beam/Ray or as standalone stereo/line-in zones where cost matters more than the 300's spatial driver array.

sonos-connect.notes: LEGACY — sold 2006–2015, no software updates or new features since May 2020 (bug/security fixes only, 'for as long as possible' per Sonos). Runs S1 controller only — cannot share a system with current S2-era gear (Amp, Port, Arc Ultra, etc.) without a split/bridged setup. Still fielded in older installs; do not spec new, and flag to the client that it's on a frozen software branch. Port counts here are from general/secondary sources, NOT freshly re-verified against a primary spec this round — confirm before relying on them; functionally it's the predecessor these numbers approximate the Port's analog+digital in/out pattern minus any HDMI (Connect predates HDMI entirely).

sonos-connect-amp.notes: LEGACY — same May-2020 software freeze as Connect above, S1-only, no HDMI (predates ARC). ~55W/ch into 8Ω (secondary-source figure, not re-verified this round). Direct functional predecessor to the current Amp, minus HDMI ARC. Still fielded; eligible for Sonos Trade Up (30% off new hardware when recycled) — worth mentioning to clients holding onto one. Do not spec new.

sonos-beam-ultra.notes: The 'Gambit' rumor made real: announced 2026-09-01, ships 2026-09-29, $699. 7.1.2 Dolby Atmos w/ dedicated up-firing drivers, redesigned center + AI Speech Enhancement, Trueplay. FCC (S59/RM059): BT + WiFi 2.4/5/6GHz 2x2. Beam Gen 2 form factor (~25.6in). PRE-SHIP entry: eARC-vs-ARC, DTS, ethernet speed, optical-adapter behavior and Sub/Era pairing all unconfirmed until spec sheets land after 9/29 — verify before spec'ing.

avpro-mxnet-sw24p.notes: Current successor to the discontinued AC-MXNET-SW24: 24x GbE PoE+ endpoint ports, 4x 10G SFP+ uplink/aggregation, 370W PoE budget. Sibling AC-MXNET-SW24E = economy Layer 2.5 variant (4x 1G SFP stacking, same 370W) for smaller deployments.
